Subject: Packet drops post VLAN swap — noisy MTU errors

Hi Mina,

We cut the segmented-VLAN swap last night (per plan) and started seeing intermittent application-level failures for a subset of endpoints that traverse the private egress path to Redwood. Symptoms:
- TCP connections established but later stall after ~120–200KB transferred
- Path MTU discovery logs show repeated ICMP frag-needed from one of your NAT nodes
- Connections not symmetric — return traffic is coming from a different SNAT IP in some cases

Attached is a short pcap capturing an affected session and our current egress NAT config snapshot. Can your team review? This started right after the cutover.

Thanks,
Alex
Network Operations
AlphaCorp

Thanks Alex — looping in Laura and Vivek from our private-deploy network team.

Quick read of the pcap shows repeated MSS clamping/ICMP frag-needed messages coming from 10.240.5.18 (one of our SNAT gateways). Two initial asks:
1) Do you have the exact cutover steps (what VLANs were moved and whether any static SNAT pools were re-assigned)?
2) Can you confirm if any intermediate firewall dropped ICMP type 3 code 4 on the path?

Proposed immediate mitigation: add an MTU clamp on the Redbridge egress interface to 1400 and pin SNAT for the affected host range to a single gateway — we can push a quick rule if you want us to try.

If you prefer, we can schedule a coordinated window tonight to apply and validate.

- Mina Haddad
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex, Mina — I pulled the NAT pool mappings. During the cutover a small subset of the SNAT pool (100 ips) was reassigned to a new gateway group to balance capacity. That could explain the asymmetric return IPs.

Action items I recommend:
- We test with a pinned SNAT (two sample IPs) for the affected subnet to confirm symmetry.
- Enable temporary MTU clamp at 1400 on the egress path for the affected flows.
- Collect conntrack counters pre/post change; I expect we may see increased conntrack entry churn which could trigger packet drops when ephemeral ports reallocate.

I can make the config change if AlphaCorp gives the green light for a 30-minute maintenance window.

Team — thanks for the quick triage. We saw the asymmetric SNATs in our app logs too. We can approve a 30-minute maintenance window at 02:00 UTC tonight (Mar 6).

Notes from our side:
- Cutover steps: moved VLAN 220 -> VLAN 420 across two top-of-rack bundles; we updated static routes but relied on autoregistration for SNAT pools (that appears to be the change).
- We do allow ICMP type 3 on edge, but not from internal infra segments — unclear if some middlebox is normalizing ICMP.

We'll upload broader traces to the Drive link once the window is confirmed. Please proceed with the pin-and-clamp plan. We'll have a NOC engineer on the call.

Date: Sat, 6 Mar 2027 14:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packet drops post VLAN swap — noisy MTU errors

All — followed the maintenance window and validated the following:
- Pinned SNAT for affected /26 to GW-5 prevented asymmetric return IPs; application failures dropped to near-zero.
- MTU clamp at 1400 on the redbridge egress fixed the ICMP frag-needed symptoms in replay tests.
- conntrack churn was high pre-change; we bumped conntrack hash buckets and tuned timeouts for short-lived flows which reduced collisions.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Keep SNAT pinning for 72 hours while we monitor (we can automate sticky SNAT mapping by workload tag).
2) Work with AlphaCorp to rollback the dynamic pool reassignment procedure during segmented-VLAN moves and add a pre-cutover SNAT sanity check.
3) Create a KB article documenting MTU clamp as an emergency mitigation for similar cutovers.

I've uploaded the validation logs and the post-change conntrack counters to the shared Drive link. If AlphaCorp wants us to revert the clamp earlier, let us know.

-Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
